name: Which Place Looks Safer? Helsingborg pairwise street-view safety
description:
Method replication: same task, scales and design as the paper; the images are not the paper's stimuli (67 new Google Street View views of Helsingborg, Sweden, captured 2017–2026, © Google). Based on Kang et al., "Human vs. AI Safety Perception? Decoding Human Safety Perception with Eye-Tracking Systems, Street View Images, and Explainable AI" (Computers, Environment and Urban Systems, 2026, doi:10.1016/j.compenvurbsys.2025.102356; preprint arXiv:2509.25457). Participants first give age group and gender, then see two street views of Helsingborg side by side and pick the one that looks safer (10 trials, images drawn without repeats). The original study collected 127 participants in Helsingborg; each image was compared about 5.8 times, and Bradley–Terry / TrueSkill-style scores give a safety score per image.

Differences from the original study: (1) no eye tracker (the original used Tobii X3-120 / 4C gaze recording; if you run one, record it separately and join on the response time stamps); (2) images are random Street View views, not the paper's 300-image set balanced across high/medium/low predicted safety; (3) online link instead of passersby at four locations in Helsingborg; (4) one closing question on familiarity with Helsingborg was added.
author: Kang, Chen, Liu, Sharma, Mazzarello, Mora, Duarte & Ratti
